description:
fixtures2/behavior/tree.fz via interp fails the full single-threaded matrix at HEAD 89db749f6 (2026-08-21). Stdout tree value and diagnostics both match exactly; ONLY the heap-stats line and the trailing byte total diverge.

  expected (tree.expected.interp.txt):  allocs 6,  bytes 288,  struct_allocs 6,  struct_bytes 288  -> 288
  actual:                               allocs 11, bytes 528,  struct_allocs 11, struct_bytes 528  -> 528

This is an UPWARD drift (+5 structs, +240 bytes) on a fixture whose output is correct, so per CLAUDE.md convention it needs masked-regression scrutiny and must NOT be reblessed. Every allocation is a struct -- no cons, closure, map, scalar-box or frame movement -- so the extra work is tuple materialization in the inc_tree recursion.

fz-d1g ('tree::{run,interp,build} newly red vs the 74-name baseline') was CLOSED, and run/build are green today; only interp is red. So either the fz-d1g fix regressed on the interp path, or it was closed on a narrower verification than all three lanes.

SUSPECTED FAMILY: the same interp-side envelope materialization isolated in fz-66j -- interp is +9 structs there where native decomposes into lanes, and this is +5 structs on a recursive tuple-returning function. Check for a shared cause before treating as independent; if it IS shared, this becomes acceptance evidence for fz-66j rather than its own fix.

REPRO: cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1 tree

comments.text:
FIXED BY fz-66j (2026-08-21) -- same root cause, confirmed by the fix rather than by inspection. tree::{run,interp,build} are all green once the interpreter reads the value layout's carrier at ProgramStep::Tuple instead of unconditionally materializing.

The +5 structs were intermediate `{:node, ...}` tuples in the inc_tree recursion that the interpreter built as heap objects and native never did. No separate work: this ticket's acceptance is the tree lanes going green in fz-66j's matrix run. Closing.

title: tree::interp allocation regression: struct_allocs 11 vs golden 6 (528 vs 288 bytes), output correct
